_meta.source: CSPI (Center for Science in the Public Interest) Chemical Cuisine Database
_meta.how_to_update: Add entries to the appropriate rating array. CSPI updates their database periodically — check their website for new evaluations. Ratings: safe, cut_back, caution, certain_people_should_avoid, avoid.
_meta.notes: CSPI is a nonprofit consumer advocacy org (est. 1971). Ratings are based on independent review of scientific literature. They accept no industry funding.

safe.name: Alginate (Alginic acid)
safe.notes: Thickener, foam stabilizer. From brown seaweed.

safe.name: Annatto
safe.notes: Natural coloring from seeds of achiote tree.

safe.name: Beta-carotene
safe.notes: Natural coloring, nutrient. Converts to Vitamin A.

safe.name: Citric acid
safe.notes: Flavoring, chelating agent. Naturally in citrus.

safe.name: Maltitol
safe.notes: Sugar alcohol. Lower calorie than sugar.

safe.name: Pectin
safe.notes: Gelling agent from fruit. Used in jams.

safe.name: Sorbitol
safe.notes: Sugar alcohol sweetener. Laxative at high doses.

safe.name: Stevia / Steviol glycosides
safe.notes: Natural high-intensity sweetener from stevia plant.

safe.name: Vanillin / Ethyl vanillin
safe.notes: Flavoring. Synthetic version of vanilla compound.

cut_back.name: High fructose corn syrup (HFCS)
cut_back.notes: Liquid sweetener. Contributes to obesity, fatty liver.

cut_back.name: Salt (Sodium chloride)
cut_back.notes: Excess linked to hypertension. Most Americans consume 50%+ over recommended limit.

cut_back.name: Sugar (Sucrose)
cut_back.notes: Excess linked to obesity, diabetes, heart disease, tooth decay.

caution.name: Artificial flavors
caution.notes: Catch-all term for hundreds of synthetic chemicals. Little safety data on mixtures.

caution.name: Caramel coloring (Classes III and IV)
caution.notes: Contains 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI), a possible carcinogen (IARC 2B). Class I/II caramel is safe.

caution.name: Carrageenan
caution.notes: Thickener from seaweed. Concerns about gut inflammation. IARC Group 3.

caution.name: Diacetyl
caution.notes: Butter flavoring. Inhalation causes bronchiolitis obliterans ('popcorn lung'). Ingestion risk unclear.

caution.name: Maltodextrin
caution.notes: Highly processed starch. Very high glycemic index (85-105).

caution.name: Modified food starch
caution.notes: Chemically treated starch. Little safety testing on specific modifications.

caution.name: Mono- and diglycerides
caution.notes: Emulsifiers. May contain trans fats not listed on nutrition labels.

caution.name: Natural flavors
caution.notes: Broadly defined. Can include processing aids and solvents. Not necessarily safer than artificial.

caution.name: Phosphates (Sodium/Calcium phosphate)
caution.notes: Excessive phosphate intake linked to kidney damage and cardiovascular risk.

caution.name: Polysorbate 60
caution.notes: Emulsifier. Some gut microbiome concerns in animal studies.

caution.name: Polysorbate 80
caution.notes: Emulsifier. Animal studies show gut barrier disruption and inflammation.

caution.name: Sucralose
caution.notes: Artificial sweetener. Some studies suggest gut microbiome disruption at high doses.

caution.name: Cellulose gum (CMC)
caution.notes: Thickener. Animal studies show gut microbiome disruption.

certain_people_should_avoid.name: Acesulfame potassium (Ace-K)
certain_people_should_avoid.notes: Artificial sweetener. Concerns about inadequacy of original safety testing.

certain_people_should_avoid.name: Aspartame
certain_people_should_avoid.notes: Artificial sweetener. Dangerous for people with PKU. IARC 2B (2023). Gut microbiome concerns.

certain_people_should_avoid.name: Carmine / Cochineal extract
certain_people_should_avoid.notes: Natural red coloring from insects. Can cause allergic reactions.

certain_people_should_avoid.name: Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
certain_people_should_avoid.notes: Flavor enhancer. Can trigger headaches, flushing in sensitive individuals.

certain_people_should_avoid.name: Mycoprotein (Quorn)
certain_people_should_avoid.notes: Can cause severe allergic reactions in some people.

certain_people_should_avoid.name: Sulfites (Sulfur dioxide)
certain_people_should_avoid.notes: Preservative. Dangerous for asthmatics — can trigger severe bronchospasm.

avoid.name: Azodicarbonamide
avoid.notes: Flour bleacher/dough conditioner. Breaks down to semicarbazide (possible carcinogen). Banned in EU/Australia.

avoid.name: Blue 1 (Brilliant Blue FCF)
avoid.notes: Synthetic dye. Inadequately tested. Possible chromosomal damage.

avoid.name: Blue 2 (Indigotine)
avoid.notes: Synthetic dye. Possible brain tumor promotion in animal studies.

avoid.name: BHA (Butylated hydroxyanisole)
avoid.notes: Antioxidant preservative. IARC 2B (possibly carcinogenic). Causes cancer in rat forestomach.

avoid.name: BHT (Butylated hydroxytoluene)
avoid.notes: Antioxidant preservative. Some studies show tumor promotion.

avoid.name: Brominated vegetable oil (BVO)
avoid.notes: Emulsifier in citrus drinks. Accumulates in body fat. FDA revoked GRAS 2024.

avoid.name: Citrus Red 2
avoid.notes: Dye for orange peels only. IARC 2B. Questionable safety.

avoid.name: DATEM (Diacetyl tartaric acid esters)
avoid.notes: Dough conditioner. Inadequately tested.

avoid.name: Dimethylpolysiloxane
avoid.notes: Anti-foaming agent (used in fryer oil). Inadequately tested for food use.

avoid.name: Green 3 (Fast Green FCF)
avoid.notes: Synthetic dye. Inadequately tested. Banned in EU.

avoid.name: Partially hydrogenated oils (trans fats)
avoid.notes: No safe level. Causes heart disease. FDA banned 2018.

avoid.name: Potassium bromate
avoid.notes: Flour treatment. IARC 2B. Causes cancer in animals. Banned in EU/UK/Canada.

avoid.name: Propyl gallate
avoid.notes: Antioxidant. IARC 2B (2023). Often used with BHA/BHT.

avoid.name: Red 3 (Erythrosine)
avoid.notes: Synthetic dye. Causes thyroid tumors in rats. FDA banned for food 2025.

avoid.name: Red 40 (Allura Red AC)
avoid.notes: Most widely used dye. Southampton Six. Accelerates tumors in mice. Linked to hyperactivity.

avoid.name: Saccharin
avoid.notes: Artificial sweetener. Historical cancer concerns. Delisted from NTP carcinogen list but CSPI maintains Avoid.

avoid.name: Sodium nitrite
avoid.notes: Curing agent. Forms carcinogenic nitrosamines. IARC 2A.

avoid.name: Sodium nitrate
avoid.notes: Curing agent. Converts to nitrite in body. Same concerns.

avoid.name: TBHQ (tert-Butylhydroquinone)
avoid.notes: Antioxidant preservative. Tumors in rats at high doses.

avoid.name: Titanium dioxide
avoid.notes: Whitening agent. EFSA: no longer safe (2021). Banned in EU. IARC 2B.

avoid.name: Yellow 5 (Tartrazine)
avoid.notes: Synthetic dye. Southampton Six. Linked to hyperactivity. Can trigger reactions in aspirin-sensitive individuals.

avoid.name: Yellow 6 (Sunset Yellow FCF)
avoid.notes: Synthetic dye. Southampton Six. Linked to hyperactivity. Contaminated with carcinogens.
